name: Hardware Security
description: Security of hardware: chips, FPGAs, PUFs, fault injection, and hardware design verification.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this listing centers on the fallout from microarchitectural speculation and side channels. Foreshadow (2018) showed that Intel SGX, a hardware trusted execution environment meant to protect secrets even from a hostile OS, could be cracked wide open by transient out-of-order execution, extracting attestation keys. Alongside it, "Translation Leak-aside Buffer" (2018) demonstrated that the TLB itself could be turned into a side channel, defeating cache-partitioning defenses. The theme of this era was clear: the very performance optimizations baked into modern CPUs were also their deepest security flaws.

The field then broadened in two directions. First, attacks moved from leaking data to corrupting it physically. SPOILER (2019) tied speculative load hazards to Rowhammer, and a sustained Rowhammer line followed, with SMASH (2021) showing synchronized many-sided hammering from JavaScript that defeats in-DRAM TRR mitigations, Half-Double (2022) reaching past adjacent rows, and ZenHammer (2024) finally porting these bit-flip attacks to AMD Zen platforms. Fault injection also went hardware-native: VoltPillager (2021) glitched SGX enclaves through the SVID voltage interface, and Light Commands (2020) injected laser-driven audio into voice assistants, expanding the physical attack surface. A parallel thread attacked machine learning hardware directly, with Terminal Brain Damage (2019) and DeepHammer (2020) using bit flips to degrade neural networks.

Second, the community responded by trying to build and verify trustworthy hardware rather than just break it. VRASED (2019) delivered a formally verified hardware/software co-design for remote attestation, HardFails (2019) catalogued why software-exploitable hardware bugs slip through verification, and PHMon (2020) offered a programmable hardware monitor for enforcing security policies. This naturally fed a wave of hardware fuzzing aimed at finding processor bugs before fabrication: TheHuzz (2022) fuzzed processor instructions against golden-reference models, and HyPFuzz (2023) combined formal methods with fuzzing for better coverage.

Where the area stands now is a tug-of-war over trusted execution and microarchitectural isolation. Branch History Injection (2022) showed hardware Spectre-v2 mitigations were not enough, AEX-Notify (2023) hardened SGX against precise single-stepping, and HECKLER (2024) broke confidential VMs using malicious interrupts. The arc runs from discovering that speculation leaks secrets, through physical fault and Rowhammer attacks that flip real bits, to a maturing practice of verifying and fuzzing hardware designs, while attackers keep finding new cracks in each generation of trusted execution.

milestones.title: Foreshadow: Extracting the Keys to the Intel SGX Kingdom with Transient Out-of-Order Execution
milestones.note: broke Intel SGX via transient execution, exposing how CPU optimizations undermine trusted execution

milestones.title: Terminal Brain Damage: Exposing the Graceless Degradation in Deep Neural Networks Under Hardware Fault Attacks
milestones.note: opened the line of hardware fault attacks targeting neural network parameters

milestones.title: VRASED: A Verified Hardware/Software Co-Design for Remote Attestation
milestones.note: delivered a formally verified hardware/software basis for trustworthy remote attestation

milestones.title: Light Commands: Laser-Based Audio Injection Attacks on Voice-Controllable Systems
milestones.note: introduced physical signal-injection by converting laser light into spoofed audio commands

milestones.title: VoltPillager: Hardware-based fault injection attacks against Intel SGX Enclaves using the SVID voltage scaling interface
milestones.note: showed hardware voltage glitching could break SGX even after software fault defenses

milestones.title: SMASH: Synchronized Many-sided Rowhammer Attacks from JavaScript
milestones.note: defeated in-DRAM TRR mitigations with synchronized Rowhammer from JavaScript

milestones.title: TheHuzz: Instruction Fuzzing of Processors Using Golden-Reference Models for Finding Software-Exploitable Vulnerabilities
milestones.note: advanced hardware design verification by fuzzing processors against golden-reference models

milestones.title: HECKLER: Breaking Confidential VMs with Malicious Interrupts
milestones.note: broke modern confidential-VM TEEs via malicious interrupts, marking the current frontier
